title: My Fiancé Wouldn't Let Me See Our Wedding Guest List. Then I Found Out He'd Invited 86 Strangers (PART 2)

blocks.text: …is marrying the love of her life with only months left to live."
I'm not dying. I'm healthy. I ran a half-marathon in the spring.

I read the invitation three times. It described a young woman with terminal cancer whose "final wish" was a beautiful wedding. It invited donors to attend the reception as honored guests and to contribute to a foundation that would "fund her treatment and carry on her legacy." My photograph was on the front. Daniel's was beside it.
The charity's name was registered three months earlier. To Daniel.

I didn't confront him. I called my cousin, who's a lawyer, and then the police. A detective named Sarah Kim took my statement that afternoon. She already knew Daniel's name. He'd done something similar two years earlier in Atlanta, under a different last name, with a different fiancée.
That woman had broken off the engagement before the wedding and never knew why her ex suddenly had money.

The plan was simple. Eighty-six wealthy donors would attend our reception thinking they were witnessing a dying woman's last wish. Daniel would give a heartbreaking speech. The money, $438,000 in "ticket sales" and pledges, would go into the foundation's account. After the honeymoon, he'd announce I was "in remission" and the foundation was "winding down."

Detective Kim asked me to go ahead with my normal routine for one more week so they could trace the accounts. It was the longest week of my life. I tasted cakes. I approved centerpieces. I kissed him goodnight.
Two days before the wedding, Daniel was arrested at his office. The foundation's account was frozen with almost all of the money still in it.
Every donor got a refund and a letter from the district attorney's office explaining what had happened.

I sent personal notes to all eighty-six of them too. Several wrote back. A retired couple in Savannah said they'd lost their own daughter to cancer and had bought tickets because my story reminded them of her. They asked if they could take me to lunch. I said yes.

Daniel pleaded guilty to wire fraud and charity fraud. I kept the wedding dress. I donated it to an organization that provides free gowns to brides who are actually facing terminal illness. It felt like the only right ending.
If you're ever unsure whether a charity is legitimate, you can check it with your state attorney general's office or a charity watchdog before donating.
